issues.description: validate_conda hardcodes Windows-only '*.exe' filter, blocking valid conda paths on macOS/Linux
issues.detail: In confpage.py the browsefile is created with `filters='*.exe'`. On macOS and Linux, conda/mamba/micromamba executables have no extension (e.g. /opt/miniconda3/bin/conda). The file dialog will hide every valid binary on non-Windows platforms, defeating the entire feature for the majority of Spyder users. The filter must be platform-aware (e.g. '*.exe' only on Windows, '*' or no filter elsewhere).

issues.description: Custom conda path is read but never validated at runtime in argv()
issues.detail: In kernelspec.py, when find_conda() returns nothing, the code falls back to `self.get_conf('conda_path', ...)` and passes it straight through to `conda_version(conda_executable=conda_exe)` and subsequent kernel-launch logic. There is no check that the configured path still exists, is executable, or is actually a conda-like binary. If the user moves/deletes the binary, or unchecks then re-enters something, kernel startup will fail far downstream with a confusing error rather than the clear 'set the path in Preferences' message. Re-running validate_conda (or at minimum os.path.isfile + X_OK) before use would fail fast with the intended message.

issues.description: validate_conda substring match is too loose and order-dependent
issues.detail: `any(tool in out.decode().lower() for tool in ['micromamba','mamba','conda'])` will accept any binary whose --version output mentions one of those substrings anywhere (including a path component or unrelated tool that prints 'conda' in its banner). It also doesn't enforce a version-string shape. A stricter regex (e.g. r'^(conda|mamba|micromamba)\s+\d') anchored to the start of stdout would be safer. Additionally, run_program may print to stderr on some platforms; the function ignores stderr entirely.

issues.description: Empty conda_path passes validation but is silently ignored when custom_conda is enabled
issues.detail: `validate_conda('')` returns True, so the user can tick 'Use a custom Conda executable' and save an empty path. At runtime, the ternary in kernelspec.py reduces to `'' or None`, which is falsy in Python, so the error message about setting a path will fire — but the preferences page accepted the inconsistent state. Either reject empty paths when custom_conda is enabled, or auto-untick custom_conda when the path is cleared, so the UI state and runtime behavior agree.

issues.description: conda_path widget is enabled at construction but no validation gate prevents apply when checkbox is on and path is blank/invalid
issues.detail: The confpage wires `custom_conda_check.checkbox.toggled.connect(conda_path.setEnabled)` and seeds the enabled state, but there is no apply_settings or is_valid hook ensuring that if 'custom_conda' is True then 'conda_path' is non-empty and validates. Users can save a half-configured state and only discover it on next kernel launch.

issues.description: run_program(...).communicate() may hang or leak the subprocess on misbehaving binaries
issues.detail: validate_conda calls `run_program(conda_executable, ['--version']).communicate()` without a timeout. If the user points at a malformed executable that waits on stdin or hangs, the preferences dialog (and validation thread) will block indefinitely. Wrap with try/finally to terminate, and pass a timeout to communicate(). Also, decoding bytes with the default codec can throw UnicodeDecodeError on exotic stdout; specify errors='replace'.

issues.description: setFocus() after select_file changes existing behavior for all browsefile widgets
issues.detail: The change in widgets/config.py adds `edit.setFocus()` inside `select_file`, which is a shared helper used by every create_browsefile callsite in Spyder. This is an unrelated UX side effect that may surprise other preference panes (focus stealing after picking a file, potentially triggering validation/blur logic elsewhere). It should either be scoped to the conda widget or called out explicitly in the PR description with a rationale.

issues.description: Configuration version not bumped despite adding new keys to main_interpreter section
issues.detail: Two new keys ('custom_conda' and 'conda_path') are added to the main_interpreter defaults in config/main.py. Spyder's config system typically requires a CONF_VERSION bump (and migration handling) when defaults change so user configs are reset/merged appropriately. Absent that, users upgrading may not see the new keys until they reset preferences, or may collide with existing stored state.

issues.description: Error message references 'Python interpreter' pane but the new section is labeled 'Conda executable'
issues.detail: The updated error string instructs users to go to 'Preferences > Python interpreter > Conda executable'. This is technically the right pane name in the codebase, but the visible group label in the screenshot reads 'Conda executable' under the Python interpreter page; verify the localized pane title matches so translations stay accurate.

`self.conda_edit = conda_path.textbox` is assigned but never referenced elsewhere in the diff. Either remove it or document why it's stored (parity with pyexec_edit suggests it may be intended for later use, but unused attributes invite confusion).

issues.description: Stylesheet 'margin-left: 3px' is a magic value with no design system reference
issues.detail: `conda_path.setStyleSheet('margin-left: 3px')` hardcodes layout spacing inline rather than using Spyder's standard spacing constants. Minor, but inconsistent with the rest of the codebase's theming and may render oddly under HiDPI scaling.

issues.description: validate_conda docstring claims it checks 'executable' bit, which is meaningless on Windows
issues.detail: `os.access(path, os.X_OK)` on Windows tests file existence, not an actual exec permission. The docstring should be qualified, or the check skipped on Windows where .exe extension is the de-facto signal. Currently harmless but misleading.

dissents.topic: Whether to validate the custom conda path at kernel-launch time

positions.position: If the preferences page already validates via validate_conda before save, re-running it on every kernel launch adds latency (a subprocess call) for a rare failure mode. Trust the configured value.

Config can drift between save and use (binary moved, env changed, file deleted). The cost of one subprocess call at kernel-launch is negligible compared to launching a kernel, and the error UX is dramatically better. Validate again.
Substring match on 'conda'/'mamba'/'micromamba' is pragmatic — handles forks, wrappers, and version-banner variations across vendors without over-fitting.

Loose matching accepts unrelated binaries whose --version output happens to contain those substrings, e.g. a script that prints its install path. A regex anchored to the start of stdout is safer and barely more code.

dissents.topic: Scope of the setFocus() change in widgets/config.py

positions.position: Adding setFocus to the shared select_file helper risks regressing other preference panes that don't expect focus changes; it should be a local override on the conda widget.
Returning focus to the edit after a file picker dismisses is generally good UX and should apply to all browsefile widgets; a global change is the right call.
Hardcoding '*.exe' is an outright bug on Linux/macOS — must be conditional on sys.platform or removed entirely.
Perhaps the filters argument is permissive and merely a default suggestion; users can switch to 'All files' in the dialog. Still suboptimal but not strictly blocking.

review.summary: The PR adds a useful fallback for users whose conda installation isn't auto-discovered, with appropriate UI plumbing. However, two issues are merge-blockers: the '*.exe' file filter is Windows-only and will hide every valid conda binary on macOS/Linux (the platforms most likely to have non-standard install paths), and the runtime path read in kernelspec.py is never re-validated, so a stale or invalid configured path produces a poor error. Several P1 concerns center on validate_conda: empty paths pass validation, the substring match is too loose, and the subprocess call has no timeout. The widgets/config.py setFocus change is a shared-helper side effect that deserves explicit justification, and the config defaults change likely needs a CONF_VERSION bump. Functionality is sound; correctness and cross-platform behavior need a second pass.
